confirmed_facts.fact: Order ORD-2003 (Smartwatch, Electronics, AED 899.00) was delivered to the customer on 2026-10-27 17:45 (+04:00).
The return was requested 2026-10-30, 2.6 days after delivery, inside the 7-day electronics window of Return v2; only Return v2 applies.
Serial SW40-60219 matches between the dispatch record, warehouse inspection and warehouse photo.
Parcel weight was 0.48 kg at pickup and 0.47 kg on receipt; dispatch weight was 0.46 kg.
Inspection records a broken strap pin with an undamaged watch body, matching the customer's statement.
Code calculated a refund amount of AED 899 (item price; delivery fees not refunded).

findings.description: The inspection (08:30 +04:00 = 04:30 UTC) and warehouse photo (08:28 +04:00) are time-stamped before the courier's delivery to the warehouse (07:10 UTC) and before WMS receipt (07:20 UTC). Only the warehouse can explain this (for example clock or time-zone setting); not settled by any record. This is a signal, not proof of who caused it.

evidence.quote: Photo of watch with broken strap pin. Serial on case back: SW40-60219

policy_references.quote: Items returned for a fault are eligible for a refund or replacement within the window if the fault is confirmed at inspection.
Missing evidence is requested from the party that holds it (seller, courier, warehouse or customer). Never assume what it would show.

findings.rationale: The return is within the Return v2 electronics window and the serial, weight and fault description are consistent. However, the inspection and photo timestamps precede the parcel's recorded arrival at the warehouse, and this has not been explained. A draft request (DRAFT-RET-2003-WAREHOUSE) asks the warehouse to confirm the correct times before any refund or replacement review.
findings.uncertainty_note: Only the timestamp conflict is open; it may be a clock or time-zone recording issue, but no record confirms that. All other checks pass. Outcome depends on the warehouse reply.
